title: AI Prompter (future job?)
author: SquareWolfGames
selftext:
Hello!

  
I want to brainstorm with the community. Basically ive been learning intensly AI usage for projects in the last 2 months (like many) and im just starting to see so much potential for me to offer my services as some kind of "AI Prompter", idea being that im a software engineer and I can probably do alot of projects that would normally be outside of my expertise now.

So my question is did you guys already think about this? Is this really a future job title (like in the next 5-10 years) I feel like alot of AI usage ends up being dependant on Human QA so it makes alot of sense to me.

I didn't go too much in details because I don't wanna give too much, I want to hear people's ideas.

comments.author: 0bscuris
comments.body:
I don’t think prompter will be a job, i think prompting ai will just be a skill that some employees are good at and some are bad at, like excel or communicating via email. 

Now possibly, there will be a job selling trainings on how to be a better prompter.

replies.author: RecklessForm
replies.body:
I'm LITERALLY doing this job RIGHT NOW, like as i'm typing this.  Prompter is absolutely a job.  The difference in token usage between someone who is good at prompting vs someone who just uses AI casually is a grand canyon, and at least for now, gets you much better results, much faster, and cheaper. (ie. using less iterations to get the desired result)

Not to toot my own horn, but the kinds of things I can get Claude to do vs some of my peers who are not paid to do what I do, is vast and pronounced.

But I also sit here all day, prompting, writing prompts the length of mini-novellas, so like any job, you get out, what you put in.

replies.author: 0bscuris
replies.body: Are people from different departments working on different projects coming to you to do the prompts for them?

replies.author: RecklessForm
replies.body:
Yes and no, for the most part no, I have my own tasks, I deal with them.  What does happen is that I have to assist others with their projects and am constantly juggling like 5-6 different projects assigned to me.  Most of what I do is essentially going down a hitlist of projects that other departments need done, but there's always roughly 20% that need "fixing" that i'm asked to assist with. 

My job, is to be basically the glue in between most projects.  So my job is not making prompts, my job is solving problems using AI.  People from other departments come to me with, we need this made to solve this.  This software needs to be able to communicate with this, etc. My job is to take those problems, and make them go away, by efficiently using AI. Prompting, skill design, and prompt structure are vastly more important than the actual contents of the prompt.  Now a days, you can tell claude to write you a good prompt, but it will often take on too much per its own thread, fill its context windows, burn its tokens chasing things it doesnt need to.  So using the right skills per thread, setting up psuedo departments within claude, delegating work to different psuedo "companies" that i've created via agents.  Thats my job.  

So in summary, I solve problems using AI, and i'm good at it, which is why I'm paid to sit here typing into claude terminals all day instead of doing actual engineering work.

replies.author: 0bscuris
replies.body:
Right. That is exactly what i said. Prompting is skill that you use to do your job, your job is building systems, one of the tools you use is ai. 

you also use emails to communicate about the problems ur fixing but emailer isn’t a job. 

I’m sure you get some emails from coworkers and before you open it you already know, this is going to be super long and full of information i don’t need and other people u know ur going to need to email them back to get more detail cuz it will be vague what they need and difficult to parse. 

That is same difference in prompt efficiency, except it’s email efficiency.

replies.author: SquareWolfGames
replies.body: That is very interesting, do you think the name of this job would be something else than prompter? Or does that fit? I see alot of people mentionning it was a thing with chatgpt 2.5 back in the days and vanished, I agree with them, but also I think im into something here.

replies.author: RecklessForm
replies.body:
Its definitely not prompter, its more of AI product designer or engineer.  

My job is not prompting, my job is using prompts, well made ones, well thought out ones, to solve problems using AI.  No one gives two shits about how beautiful my prompts are, they do care intensely about my output, and (incredibly stupidly) how many tokens i'm burning.  I often get lil emails like, you're not using enough tokens, something wrong?  Like, WTF, i'm not using enough tokens because i'm good at my job, lol.

replies.author: SquareWolfGames
replies.body: oh yeah... the token part is crazy, I heard my boss talk about it, he is in web dev.

replies.author: RecklessForm
replies.body: Yeah, not just me, i have friends who do programming on the healthcare side.  They are constantly getting hounded about not using enough tokens.  Like, somehow the C-suite has gotten it all up in their heads that the only measuring stick is token usage, therefore, throw all of the companies money into a big bonfire, and we'll see how hot this fire can get, before it burns the building down!

replies.author: blueeetherabbit
replies.body:
hmm not saying you're not productive enough.. But what's your flow like? I burnt through 75% of my weekly Claude budget in 3 days business days, they had to hook me up with a Codex seat to keep me busy or I would've taken some days of work off lol

I'm working on multiple projects at once, each dockerized node instances with frontend and APIs running locally. All my tasks are performed by multiple agents and in parallel as much as possible, and I perform a decently robust self-review on all my work before I send it out for any external agent reviews.

comments.author: Virtual-Bottle-8604
comments.body: People tried to market themselves as prompt engeneer and got laughed into oblivion. Youre doing the easiest lowest effort hobby in the world at the moment. No one will pay you for it.

comments.author: aicis
comments.body: Prompting is just something you do to interact with a tool. There is no job called "button pusher", is there?

comments.author: EliasWick
comments.body:
At the release of public LLMs people had to know way to abuse the AI and get great results. Nowadays you don't need the same level of experience.

If you want a good job in game dev, you need to become really good at one thing and know a bunch of other things. The competition is hard, especially if you just are getting started.

comments.author: Negative-Tear5402
comments.body:
There was a brief period where people thought this was the future of AI and humans. Where a whole career of people who specialized in prompting the AI would arise. But that lasted all of 2 months.

Short answer, no.

Entrepreneurs keep creating AI Wrappers and try to sell it as a new type of business. But a couple months later, the major AI companies solve that problem and do it 100x better and make those wrappers obselete.

AI companies know that the average user is really bad at prompting. So they specifically target that point and develop the next model to bridge that gap.

I get what you're trying to say, but this is something AI companies are fully aware of and are spending a lot of their own money, time, energy in solving it.

comments.author: blueeetherabbit
comments.body: I'm a software eng currently. I think I see a future where software eng + project manager + design + qa merge into one position again (anyone remember the webmaster?) into a sort of Product Engineer role. Or at least at my job this is basically becoming expected of all developers. We went from working on a single ticket at a time, to managing entire projects and features on our own

replies.author: SquareWolfGames
replies.body: Exactly! Im really unsure about calling it AI Prompter, it does feel like a crazy multi-role in one person. And that is kind of the service I think could be interesting for people who know nothing about tech but want an app, a game, a business, etc.. for cheap.

replies.author: blueeetherabbit
replies.body:
Who knows if that will even need to be a thing. People like Elon think the future will be you just asking your phone to do whatever we want and were so close to that, I really believe him.  


We're maybe a year or two away from being able to pick up my phone and go: "Hey Siri make me a 6 page brochure app/site for my business, grab the best photos from my album/cloud, you've already got all my details, testimonials, texts, emails, receipts and years of history on my device, so go to town and make it look nice. Have a merch page too. When its done share the url with my family on iMessage"

  
This would be ezpz for someone in the Apple ecosystem, ecommerce would fit real nice into Apple Pay too. And we all know how Apple is always a bit late to the game, but will manage to capture a huge portion of the world, its marketing, and direction of its competitors with what they decide to do.

  
Why would they need to pay someone a salary to do that? Games are only a few steps behind this.

comments.author: Negative-Tear5402
comments.body:
To add to my previous comment:

Matt Pocock solves the Ai prompting problem. He's a senior software engineer who created a Skill for vibe coding that helps keep projects in line:

  
[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M6mYodf0dJM&t=908s](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M6mYodf0dJM&t=908s)

  
I don't want to crush your idea, because who knows, maybe one day you'll figure out a really useful addon that nobody thought of. But the reality of it, there are thousands of people with your skillset who do it for free and make it public.

comments.author: Hot-Middle7260
comments.body: No. Good prompting was relevant years ago during GPT 2.5 era but now models especially frontiers can operate beyond needing good “prompts”

comments.author: robhanz
comments.body:
I don't think "prompter" will become a job.

I think the job will be "solving problems", and prompting skill will be one of the things that goes into it.  The loop between design and implementation will close.  That's what I see happening going forward.

I think you can sold it ,to people that is completly blind to tecnology or AI .In the end the good cook know the best ingredients and how to check their quality.

replies.author: SquareWolfGames
replies.body:
Exactly, its more for the common public, because most people don't realise how big of a gap there is between us and me and them. They don't know how to use AI even if we think its easy.

And It would be very individualized and I think alot of people would rather talk to a human for these projects.

comments.author: Relative-Coat9691
comments.body:
Making products or at least part of the products , flows and pipelines.  Tuning and presenting finished ready to use reliable pipelines maybe.  
job = something that takes effort and skill. Prompting is very low bar

models and harnesses already do prompting themselves and do it better every day.   
creating something is not an issue. Iterating something into useful product is

replies.author: SquareWolfGames
replies.body: Yeah exactly, the job would be to iterate on a project, not just do the bare minimum
